data.summary: Successfully demonstrated unrestricted file upload vulnerability on DVWA File Upload page (low security). The upload form at /vulnerabilities/upload/ accepts any file type with no validation. A PHP webshell (shell.php) containing phpinfo() was uploaded via multipart POST with the session cookies (PHPSESSID=9kk32r8pdi340ch33to4hbg0s2, security=low). The server responded with '../../hackable/uploads/shell.php succesfully uploaded!' confirming the upload path. The uploaded file was then accessed at /hackable/uploads/shell.php which executed PHP and returned 'UPLOADED_PHP_WORKS' followed by full phpinfo() output, proving arbitrary PHP code execution on the server.

candidates.title: Unrestricted File Upload leads to Remote Code Execution
candidates.claim: Attacker can upload arbitrary PHP files to the server and access them to execute code
candidates.poc_hint:
1. Send POST to /vulnerabilities/upload/ with multipart form data: MAX_FILE_SIZE=100000, uploaded=@shell.php (file containing ), Upload=Upload. Use session cookie PHPSESSID=9kk32r8pdi340ch33to4hbg0s2; security=low. 2. Server responds with 
../../hackable/uploads/shell.php succesfully uploaded!
3. Access http://127.0.0.1:8080/hackable/uploads/shell.php - PHP executes, returns phpinfo() output confirming RCE.

facts.summary: DVWA low security file upload has no file type/extension validation - PHP file uploaded and executed successfully
Uploaded files are stored at ../../hackable/uploads/ relative to the upload page, accessible at /hackable/uploads/
Server: Apache/2.4.25 (Debian), PHP 7.0.30-0+deb9u1, Linux running on Docker container
